scenario: Kimi 2.0.1 isolated public CLI install, readback, doctor, unchanged re-add, changed-byte refresh, guarded failure, recovery, and removal

regressions.before: Kimi recorded /private/tmp/.../plugins/managed/personal while plgnz expected /tmp/.../plugins/managed/personal; lexical comparison rejected the successful native install and rollback removed the new registry row.
regressions.after: Existing recorded and expected roots are compared by filesystem identity; the canonical alias is accepted.

regressions.before: Kimi recorded native id personal while the plgnz install ledger expected personal@personal; public add failed post-install readback with native install readback is missing personal@personal.
regressions.after: Kimi keeps the bare native id and plgnz exposes the validated marker-owned logical id personal@personal for list, doctor, update, and remove.

stdout: kimi  ✓  install 'personal@personal' source and native content match their recorded byte proofs
kimi  !  install 'personal@personal' staleness unknown — cannot determine head of <isolated-root>/collection

calls.setup: Append a public fixture line to one source skill.
calls.readback: The appended fixture line was present in the active managed copy.

calls.setup: Add an unsupported hooks field to the source root manifest.
calls.stderr: Kimi root manifest hooks is unsupported without an explicit native declaration
calls.readback: The active skill bytes had the same SHA-256 before and after the refused add.

calls.setup: Restore the valid source manifest; this also resolves the durable pending install intent left by the expected failed add.

limits: This probe used explicit isolated Kimi and plgnz homes and did not mutate a real user home or fleet installation.
It proves the native public CLI lifecycle, registry/readback identity, content protection, and removal behavior without a model request.
It does not prove model-time skill selection, command execution, MCP execution, or other full-session semantics.
Kimi's native remove endpoint removed the registry row and retained the managed cache directory; plgnz does not hand-edit that native cache.
